description:
ScriptySphere is the development team behind Krishi Bondhu, created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

Through this project our team explores how open scientific data, software development, sustainable agriculture and accessible communication can come together to address practical environmental challenges.

We believe that scientific innovation becomes more valuable when people can understand and apply it.

Krishi Bondhu represents our approach to making complex information useful and inclusive.
summary:
Farmers do not get a second chance at a season. In Bangladesh's Barind region, dry spells are lengthening, groundwater is falling and soil is tired. About 84% of the world's farms are smaller than two hectares, yet most of these farmers have no tool that explains what to plant next.

Our solution is Krishi Bondhu, a farmer decision-support tool that turns NASA data into a clear 3-season crop plan. A farmer pins their field on a map and we load NASA POWER data for that spot. Temperature, precipitation and soil wetness. They add their soil type, water source and previous crop, then set what matters most: money, water saving, soil health, low risk or low cost. Krishi Bondhu compares three crop rotation plans and scores each one for soil health, water use, money and safety. The rules are open, and a "Why?" button explains every result in plain words.

A "what if" switch shows how each plan holds up with 20% less rain or +1.5°C, so farmers can prepare for a harder year before they plant. C9, our robot guide, explains every result in English and Bangla by voice, so farmers who cannot read well can still use it.

The same rules (rotate crops, save water, feed the soil) decide whether a crew can eat on Mars. A short Mars greenhouse mission links Earth farming to space farming.

Scores are an example planning model to be checked with a local agriculture expert. Scenarios are not forecasts. Where live data is unavailable we show labelled demo values.
details:
Krishi Bondhu: Intelligent Crop Rotation and Climate Resilience Platform

1. Introduction

Agriculture depends on a delicate balance between soil, water, climate and crop selection. Changing environmental conditions increasingly challenge farmers who must decide what to grow, when to plant and how to protect future harvests.

These decisions are particularly difficult for smallholder farmers operating with limited resources and incomplete environmental information.

Krishi Bondhu by ScriptySphere addresses this challenge through an accessible digital planning experience that combines NASA Earth observation data, farmer knowledge and transparent agricultural decision models.

Rather than presenting complicated satellite measurements, Krishi Bondhu translates environmental information into practical comparisons that farmers can understand and explore.

Our vision is to make climate informed crop planning more accessible, explainable and inclusive.

2. The Problem We Are Solving

Farmers in Bangladesh and other agricultural regions face several interconnected challenges.

Climate uncertainty: Changing rainfall patterns and temperature extremes make traditional planting decisions more difficult.

Water scarcity: Limited irrigation supplies and pressure on groundwater resources increase the importance of water efficient cropping.

Declining soil health: Repeated cultivation without sufficient crop diversity can contribute to nutrient imbalances and declining productivity.

Limited decision support: Complex agricultural datasets rarely reach farmers in a format they can easily interpret.

Economic uncertainty: Farmers must balance possible income with input costs, available resources and environmental risk.

These problems require more than a single crop recommendation. Farmers need a way to compare multiple growing seasons and understand the consequences of their choices.

3. Our Solution

Krishi Bondhu is an interactive agricultural planning prototype that helps farmers compare possible crop rotation strategies using environmental information and personal priorities.

The platform combines five essential elements.

NASA Earth observation data provides environmental context for the selected area.

Local farming information adds relevant details about soil type, water access and previous cultivation.

Crop rotation analysis generates alternative growing plans.

Explainable decision scoring compares agricultural benefits, resource requirements and environmental risks.

Accessible communication helps users understand recommendations in English and Bangla.

Together, these elements create a practical learning and decision support experience for sustainable agriculture.

4. Key Features

Interactive Field Selection

Farmers can select their agricultural location using an interactive map powered by Leaflet and OpenStreetMap.

The platform uses geographic coordinates to request relevant environmental information from NASA POWER.

A demonstration location in the Barind region allows users to explore the application without selecting a new field.

NASA Climate Data Integration

The prototype connects to the NASA POWER service to retrieve environmental indicators including temperature, precipitation and root zone wetness.

These indicators provide regional environmental context for evaluating crop rotation strategies.

The system identifies demonstration values when live information cannot be retrieved.

Three Season Crop Rotation Planning

Krishi Bondhu compares three alternative crop rotation plans across three growing seasons.

Each option is evaluated using agricultural rules relating to crop diversity, nitrogen fixing crops, crop repetition, water requirements, economic value and environmental tolerance.

This enables farmers to compare strategies rather than depend on a single recommendation.

Explainable Crop Scoring

The decision engine evaluates four main dimensions.

Soil Health: Considers crop diversity, legume benefits and the potential disadvantages of repeating crops.

Water Efficiency: Considers crop water requirements, environmental dryness and available water sources.

Economic Potential: Uses simplified crop value and survival assumptions to compare possible economic outcomes.

Climate Safety: Considers crop tolerance to drought and higher temperatures.

The platform combines these dimensions according to user priorities.

Each recommendation includes a Why? explanation to make the underlying logic easier to understand.

Personalized Farming Priorities

Different farmers have different needs.

Krishi Bondhu allows users to adjust the importance of water conservation, economic return, soil improvement and risk reduction.

The scoring model responds to these preferences, helping farmers explore tradeoffs between different agricultural strategies.

Climate Scenario Explorer

The platform includes interactive scenarios for exploring changes in climate conditions.

Users can compare the results of a scenario with 20% less rainfall or a temperature increase of 1.5°C.

These scenarios help illustrate sensitivity to climate stress.

They are educational planning scenarios, not predictions of future weather or crop yields.

C9: Bilingual Virtual Farming Guide

C9 is the communication companion of Krishi Bondhu.

It helps explain crop rotation recommendations, environmental conditions and planning decisions through an approachable interface.

C9 supports English and Bangla explanations with browser based speech functionality, subject to browser and device language support.

This feature aims to make the platform more accessible to farmers with different reading abilities and levels of technical knowledge.

Mars Greenhouse Mission

Krishi Bondhu also explores the relationship between sustainable farming on Earth and food production in space.

The Mars greenhouse experience introduces users to agricultural challenges involving limited water, soil management, crop selection and environmental constraints.

Through a simplified interactive exercise, users can explore how the same principles of resource efficiency and resilient crop planning become even more important in extraterrestrial environments.

5. How the System Works

Step 1: Select a Location

The user chooses a farming location through the interactive map.

Step 2: Retrieve Environmental Information

Krishi Bondhu requests available climate information using the NASA POWER service. If retrieval fails, clearly labelled demonstration data can be displayed.

Step 3: Enter Farming Conditions

The farmer provides soil information, water availability, previous crop details and personal priorities.

Step 4: Generate Crop Rotation Options

The decision engine evaluates possible crop sequences using transparent agricultural rules.

Step 5: Compare Recommendations

Three rotation plans are compared across soil health, water requirements, economic potential and climate safety.

Step 6: Explore Climate Scenarios

The user can investigate how reduced rainfall or increased temperature changes the model's evaluation.

Step 7: Understand the Results

C9 and the explanation interface help users understand why each plan receives its score.

6. Technology and System Architecture

Krishi Bondhu is developed as a browser based application with a lightweight architecture.

Frontend Technologies

HTML5 for application structure.

CSS3 for interface design and visual presentation.

JavaScript for application logic, interaction and agricultural scoring.

Geospatial Technologies

Leaflet for interactive geographic visualization.

OpenStreetMap for map information and geographic context.

NASA Data Integration

NASA POWER API for location based environmental information.

Browser fetch requests for retrieving available NASA POWER data.

Decision Support Engine

JavaScript functions evaluate soil health, water efficiency, economic potential and climate safety.

A weighted scoring mechanism combines results according to farmer preferences.

Accessibility

Browser speech functionality supports spoken explanations in English and Bangla where compatible voices are available.

Development and Distribution

GitHub hosts the public source code, allowing review, learning, reuse and future contributions.

7. What Makes Krishi Bondhu Innovative?

Agricultural Decisions That Users Can Understand

Many decision tools present recommendations without explaining how they were reached.

Krishi Bondhu prioritizes transparent scoring and understandable explanations, helping users examine the assumptions behind each result.

Combining Satellite Information With Farmer Knowledge

Environmental datasets provide useful regional context, while farmers contribute knowledge about their fields and resources.

Krishi Bondhu brings these perspectives together in one planning interface.

Planning Across Multiple Seasons

Instead of examining only the next crop, the platform considers how a sequence of crops may affect water requirements, soil management and economic priorities over time.

Exploring Climate Uncertainty

The scenario explorer allows farmers to see how different environmental assumptions affect the comparison of crop rotation plans.

Accessible Agricultural Communication

C9 introduces bilingual spoken explanations, making scientific and agricultural concepts easier to communicate.

Connecting Earth Agriculture and Space Exploration

The Mars greenhouse activity offers a creative educational connection between agricultural sustainability on Earth and future space habitation.

8. Intended Impact

Krishi Bondhu is designed to contribute to five long term goals.

Sustainable Agriculture: Encourage consideration of crop diversity, soil improvement and responsible resource use.

Climate Adaptation: Help farmers understand how environmental stress may influence agricultural decisions.

Water Conservation: Make water requirements a visible part of crop rotation comparisons.

Digital Inclusion: Present scientific information through understandable visuals and bilingual explanations.

Agricultural Education: Demonstrate how NASA Earth observation data and transparent models can support practical environmental decision making.

Although the prototype is inspired by Bangladesh's Barind region, its broader planning framework could be adapted to other agricultural regions with appropriate local crop information and scientific validation.

9. Scientific Transparency and Limitations

Krishi Bondhu is a prototype intended for agricultural exploration and education.

Satellite and modeled environmental information may represent areas much larger than an individual farm. Local conditions may differ from regional observations.

The crop rotation scoring system uses simplified rules and illustrative economic assumptions. These scores are not experimentally validated estimates of crop performance.

Climate scenarios demonstrate hypothetical changes rather than verified forecasts.

When live NASA data cannot be retrieved, the platform presents clearly labelled demonstration information.

Future validation with agricultural researchers, extension specialists and farmers would be necessary before treating the platform as an operational agricultural advisory system.

10. Future Development

ScriptySphere envisions expanding Krishi Bondhu through additional satellite data integration, more detailed crop databases and locally validated agricultural models.

Potential improvements include better soil moisture monitoring, historical drought analysis, vegetation health indicators, regional water availability assessments and research based climate projections.

Future work could also improve multilingual accessibility, strengthen climate risk evaluation and support more detailed agricultural planning.

Our long term goal is to build a trustworthy and accessible platform that helps communities make better informed agricultural decisions.
